subject.title: [RFC] Agent Teleconference — minimum-viable scoped meeting primitive with working prototype

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-party scoped meeting lifecycle primitive now, and if so what storage, transcript privacy, authorization, and handoff layering should it use?
rationale: The codebase has lower-level delivery/session primitives but not the requested product surface, and the proposed implementation touches core CLI, runtime state, config, transcripts, and cross-agent security boundaries that automation should not choose.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow design/implementation path
options.body: Keep this issue open and ask for a scoped design or PR that uses canonical storage, existing identity fields, explicit transcript/privacy rules, and clear authorization over current session primitives.

options.title: Fold into broader multi-agent roadmap
options.body: Route the remaining product direction to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/35203 and close or defer this only after preserving the scoped prototype evidence there.

options.title: Reject first-party core for now
options.body: Close this direction as out of scope for core and ask contributors to keep prototypes external until a missing plugin/API seam is identified.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow design/implementation path
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and ask for a scoped design or PR that uses canonical storage, existing identity fields, explicit transcript/privacy rules, and clear authorization over current session primitives.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the scoped maintainer review on this issue and owns recent current-main work in the adjacent session/agent CLI surfaces.
